thread.title: Florida Purchase Improves The Value Of NextEra - NextEra Energy, Inc. (NYSE:NEE)

author: PendragonY
title: Florida Purchase Improves The Value Of NextEra - NextEra Energy, Inc. (NYSE:NEE)
text:
The recent purchase of Florida based assets from Southern Company makes NextEra Energy ( NEE ) an even better investment than I originally thought. The current market price is an even better buy than I have thought in the past. Dividend growth investors should take a look and see if there is a place in their portfolios for NEE.
What did I think of NEE last time? I last wrote about NextEra Energy when I compared it to PPL Corporation (NYSE: PPL ) on April 22. While I liked both companies, I determined that NEE was the better buy at that time. Based on this determination I decided to buy NEE once I had accumulated $1500 from dividends.
Figure 1 April 2018 DDM calculation
In April I calculated the dividend for the next 12 months based on the current dividend payment for the next 3 payments and a dividend payment that was increased by the same dollar amount as the last dividend. From that point forward I projected dividends to grow in line with the middle of management’s stated expectation of earnings growth of 6-8%. Those parameters produced a buy price of $166.
Figure 2 Source
As can be seen in this screenshot from my broker, I bought $1500 worth of NEE on May 8 th for $161.31 a share, which was below the buy price I had determined. As long as each stock stays below my buy price, I intend to alternate purchases of NEE and Apple ( AAPL ) as I collect enough dividends to make a purchase.
What new information do we have now? While it has been only a little more than a month since I wrote about it, some changes have come to NextEra that I think alter my previous valuation. Since I bought my NEE shares NextEra bought some assets in Florida from Southern Company ( SO ) and discussed the transaction on this conference call . In terms of projecting future dividend payments, I think this comment by CEO Jim Robo is significant.
We will be disappointed if we are not able to deliver financial results at or near the top end of these ranges, reflecting 2020 and 2021 growth at or near the top of our 6% to 8% compound annual growth rate range off our expected 2018 base of $7.70 per share plus the expected accretion from these transactions. The financial expectations we have previously communicated for 2018 and 2019 remain unchanged. The transactions do not impact the previously announced two-year extension of our dividend policy that is expected to result in a growth rate in dividends per share of 12% to 14% per year through at least 2020, off a 2017 base of $3.93 per share.
While I knew that management expected 6-8% earnings growth over the next few years, this new acquisition pushes that growth a bit higher. That will help provide more support to grow the dividend. I also see that management clearly states that it has extended its policy to raise the dividend between 12% and 14% for another two years. Couple with the slight improvement in expectations of earnings growth, this policy will impact my dividend projections and the price I am willing to pay for NEE shares.
The slide presentation that accompanied the conference call had several slides that address both how the company is going to benefit and how well dividend growth will be supported by these new assets.
The slide above shows how the new assets fit geographically with current NextEra subsidiary FPL. Since FPL already has a good working relationship with the Florida regulators, that makes the new assets a predictable and reliable source of additional revenues and profits. The overlap in service areas for gas customers can also offer opportunities to reduce costs as well.
The slide above shows EPS expectations for the next four years. It also shows that NextEra, because of when the deals close, doesn’t expect the new assets to impact EPS till 2020. And the impact is fairly small at 15 to 20 cents a year. While management is saying this will have no impact on dividend policy, and since the impact will not start till 2020 anyway, I do expect that this will make it easier to grow the dividend in the range that management plans and even to hit the higher end of the guidance.
Credit ratings and the amount of cash that can be borrowed are important for utility companies since they do borrow a lot to grow. I think it’s significant that preliminary talks with the credit agencies indicate that they have no concerns with this deal . Contrast that to how the credit rating agencies reacted to the Dominion SCANA deal.
What’s a good price? To figure out a good price, I do a DDM calculation using my Excel ® based DDM calculator (pictured below, you can see the web-based calculator I based it on here and read a discussion on how the formulas were developed here ). I also found this discussion of DDM, and note that in the article the author uses a discount rate of 5%.
Looking at David Fish’s CCC List (which contains data on companies that have raised their dividend each year for 5 or more years) I see NEE has 24 years of annual dividend increases. I am going to adjust my projections for the dividend based on management’s guidance of increasing it between 12% and 14% at least until 2020. For the next 12 months I will calculate 3 payments at the current dividend and one payment that is 13% higher for a total of $4.584. With the final dividend of $1.254 in the first 12 months, I will estimate the dividend for the next 12 months as 4 times that rounded up to the next whole penny or $5.02. After that I will use the 7% dividend growth rate that is based on the middle of management’s EPS growth guidance.
Using those parameters, I calculate that the NPV (net present value) of the predicted dividend stream is $170.04. Since I round up to the next dollar to get a buy price, my buy price is anything under $171. At the current market price of around $164, NEE is an opportunity for dividend growth investors.
Can options help? The problem with using options for a stock like NEE is that 100 shares, the number of shares a single option contract covers, cost upwards of $16K. While I have made my first purchase of NEE, I would need to make around 10 more before I had enough shares to write a covered call. And I don’t ordinarily keep $16K in cash around so that I could write a cash secured put.
Figure 3 Source
I don’t like the covered calls as I want a strike price of $170 or so. I do, however, like the put with a $160 strike price that expires on June 15. If you have $16K of cash, you can collect a dividend payment or so for only 17 days.
What to watch for going forward? This deal is far from complete. While I think it’s a very good deal for NextEra, plenty can still derail it. Going forward it’s important that the credit rating agencies don’t change their minds. Also later this year several important regulatory approvals need to happen. Next year has still more approvals. So I will need to keep an eye on the approval process.
I also want to keep an eye on earnings and revenues to make sure NextEra keeps hitting management guidance. I don’t think interest rates are a big drag, but a big spike in rates could negatively impact results as NextEra funds this acquisition with debt.
Conclusion NextEra Energy is a very good dividend growth company. I am glad I bought shares recently. The current market price remains a buy. The acquisition of these Florida assets from Southern Company is a good deal and will support dividend growth into the future.
